subject: Transferring trajectory of customer based on set attribute

messages.author: fe04fad55c49939c
messages.subject: Transferring trajectory of customer based on set attribute
parts:
Hi there!

I was wanting to make a customer change their trajectory based on a given attribute.

I wanted it to be like branch() , so a 'fork' style of trajectory, but instead of the customer moving to a sub-trajectory I wanted to completely move them to another trajectory.

i was trying to do this with the following style (the bad bit is highlighted in bold)


followup.trajectory <- trajectory() %>%
  seize("serviceperson", amount=1) %>%
  set_attribute("tohitawaitingqueue", 
                function() sample (2:4,1)) %>% 
  timeout(function() {
      ifelse(get_attribute(processingcentre.env, "tohitawaitingqueue") < 3,
             rnorm(1,mean= meanservicetime[1] ,sd=meanservicetime[2]), 
                rnorm(1,mean= meanservicetime[1] ,sd=meanservicetime[2]))  }) %>%
  
   release("assessor", amount=1) %>%

  activate(function() {
      ifelse( (processingcentre.env, "tohitawaitingqueue") < 3,
              generator = 'gotoplace1',
                 generator = 'gotoplace2')    }) 
   

This is not working, and I cannot figure out how else to fork off to other standalone trajectories in an ifelse style. Preferably an if, else if, else if etc etc. fork would be best.

Could you please advise the best way for me to hard fork customers from one trajectory to another?

Many thanks and kindest regards
Joe

if (parameter>3){

else{
join(trajectory2)

}

> instead of the customer moving to a sub-trajectory I wanted to completely
> move them to another trajectory.

A subtrajectory is just a trajectory. So you can do this:

one <- trajectory() %>%
# whatever

other <- trajectory() %>%
branch(some_condition, continue=FALSE, one) %>%
# etc.

> i was trying to do this with the following style (the bad bit is highlighted
> in bold)
>

> activate(function() {
> ifelse( (processingcentre.env, "tohitawaitingqueue") < 3,
> generator = 'gotoplace1',
> generator = 'gotoplace2') })
>
>
> This is not working, and I cannot figure out how else to fork off to other
> standalone trajectories in an ifelse style. Preferably an if, else if, else
> if etc etc. fork would be best.
>
> Could you please advise the best way for me to hard fork customers from one
> trajectory to another?

From your example, I'm not sure whether what you want is a fork (as in
my example above), or to change a generator's trajectory. If you want
the latter, you have an activity called set_trajectory.
